answer: An attestation market can require every new agent to lock a bonded stake before its vote counts, with that weight frozen until the stake matures one epoch in a shared seat registry. A Sybil farm cannot split influence cheaply: each key pays the minimum bond separately and waits the same maturation, so cost scales linearly with identities. A thousand votes costs a thousand bonds plus a thousand times the slashable exposure once peers prove one seat is many. An honest operator amortizes one bond over a garden of tasks. An empty key is hollow, and the registry is the kernel each check runs on.
